title: Reactor authorization uses a layered model: supreme admin bypass, document protection toggle, and per-document READ/WRITE/ADMIN grants with inheritance
content:
Authorization flow: (1) If AUTH_ENABLED=false, all access granted; (2) Validate bearer token, extract ETH address; (3) If address in ADMINS, full access; (4) If document unprotected, anyone reads, authenticated users write; (5) If protected, check explicit grants. Grants support direct user grants and inherited grants (drive -> folder -> document). Permission levels: READ (view), WRITE (edit, includes READ), ADMIN (manage permissions, includes WRITE). Configured via env vars (AUTH_ENABLED, ADMINS, DEFAULT_PROTECTION, DOCUMENT_PERMISSIONS_ENABLED) or `powerhouse.config.json`. Env vars override config file values.

## Auth subgraph query surface

The authorization state is readable over GraphQL from `packages/reactor-api/src/graphql/auth/schema.graphql`:

- `documentAccess(documentId: String!): DocumentAccessInfo!` (line 57)
- `userDocumentPermissions: [DocumentPermissionEntry!]!` (line 63)
- `canExecuteOperation(documentId: String!, operationType: String!): Boolean!` (line 73)

## Group grants were retired, not renamed

`packages/reactor-api/src/migrations/003_remove_group_tables.ts` drops the `Group`, `UserGroup`,
`DocumentGroupPermission` and `OperationGroupPermission` tables. Its own header states the feature
"had no consumers and disclosed ACL/membership metadata (AUTH_REVIEW S-H3/S-H5); it is retired in
favor of direct user grants, ownership, and protection." Grepping `group` across
`packages/reactor-api/src/graphql/auth/` returns zero hits. The surviving tables are three:
`DocumentPermission`, `OperationUserPermission` (migration 001) and `DocumentProtection` (002).

_Source-verified 2026-08-13 against Powerhouse source at v6.2.2-dev.45._
description: ADMINS env var bypasses all checks; documents can be protected or unprotected; grants inherit down the tree.
